bloat_trajectory.notes: Single-concept cycle: 138 production LOC (constants + serde attrs + 5-line reject branch + 2 services field passes). Test LOC is 2.7x production, which is deliberate investment, not bloat. No abstractions added; one dead constant pre-disclosed as R4.

evidence.observation: schema_version now exists in two places of the same serialized envelope: on CounterexampleBundleRecord (envelope, line 206, declared authoritative by the field doc at lines 202-204) and on CounterexampleBundleSummary (nested, line 178). Nothing structurally enforces their equality: save() overwrites both unconditionally (lines 234-235), but any future writer path that deserializes a summary from elsewhere, or a new summary type embedded in another envelope, can carry a summary whose schema_version disagrees with the envelope. The loader rejects only on record.schema_version (line 293); a mismatched summary.schema_version would silently pass.

findings.impact: Redundant version fields create two sources of truth inside one serialized blob. Today save() canonicalizes both so drift cannot be persisted through the public API; the residual risk is a future code path constructing records by hand (e.g. a migration tool) that sets summary.schema_version independently, which the loader would not detect.

remediation.action: Either (a) drop summary.schema_version when a wire-format break is acceptable, or (b) add a loader-side assertion that record.schema_version == summary.schema_version, returning StoreError::Serialization on mismatch. Option (b) is a 3-line change at the site of the existing >CURRENT check (line 293).

details.rationale: Both fields are written by exactly one canonical writer today (D5 overwrite), so severity MEDIUM (latent drift risk, not active divergence) and remediation backlog (no failure path exists now).

evidence.observation: The cycle deliberately ships an asymmetric contract: load_counterexample_bundle hard-rejects schema_version > CURRENT (line 293) while list_counterexample_bundles best-effort includes future-versioned rows (pinned by test m9_01_list_includes_future_versioned_row_best_effort, lines ~880-982 of the new tests; verify disclosure R2 confirms). Additionally, the reject is implemented as StoreError::Serialization with a human upgrade message, which is an error-kind overload: callers pattern-matching on Serialization to catch corrupt blobs will also catch the forward-compatibility rejection.

findings.impact: Two distinct failure semantics (corrupt blob vs future writer) collapse into one error variant. This is disclosed and deliberate (R2 + module docs), and the asymmetry is arguably the right product call for a best-effort list path; the cost is that upstream consumers cannot distinguish 'data corrupt' from 'written by newer chronos' without string-matching the message. verify-report W1-independent: this does not affect current behaviour (only one schema version exists).

remediation.action: When a second schema version actually ships (the first v2 bump), introduce a dedicated StoreError variant (e.g. SchemaTooNew { found, supported }) or a distinguished error code so callers can branch without message parsing.

details.rationale: No behavioural failure today; the semantic compression becomes costly exactly when versioning starts to matter.

evidence.observation: KNOWN_BUNDLE_SCHEMA_VERSIONS (&[u32] = &[1]) is declared with #[allow(dead_code)] and referenced by nothing: grep across all crates returns exactly one hit (its own declaration). The loader policy (D3) checks only the upper bound record.schema_version > CURRENT (line 293). The constant exists to let future cycles 'tighten the check without a new lint cascade' (own doc comment), which is explicitly speculative. Verify disclosure R4 already records it honestly.

findings.impact: 3 LOC of speculative generality plus a suppression that will outlive its justification if the tightening never happens; every future reader pays a small comprehension tax to learn it is intentionally inert. No runtime cost (const slice, optimized out).

remediation.action: Either delete the constant and re-add it at the v2 bump (a 1-line re-addition, the lint cascade argument is weak for a single item), or wire it into the loader when the first non-contiguous version set exists (e.g. accept 1 and 3 but not 2). Prefer deletion: YAGNI. loc_reducible: 3; change_risk: LOW.
